item.title: Oncological and quality-of-life outcomes after robotic versus open neck dissection in oral cavity cancer: a prospective matched-pair analysis.
item.dc:creator: Gupta K, Popat S, Sarin D
item.description:
Authors: Gupta K, Popat S, Sarin D
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108185
Published: 2026-Oct-16
PMID: 42887359



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neck dissection remains the standard of care for regional control of nodal disease in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma, but the conventional trans-cervical approach leaves a visible scar and carries a recognized risk of shoulder morbidity. Remote-access robotic neck dissection has been proposed as a means of preserving oncological adequacy while improving cosmetic and functional outcomes. We report a prospective matched-pair comparison of retro-auricular robotic neck dissection and standard open neck dissection in patients with oral cavity cancer. METHODS: Sixty-four patients undergoing neck dissection for oral cavity carcinoma between January 2020 and December 2025 were enrolled and matched 1:1 by age, sex, tumour subsite and clinical stage; 32 underwent retro-auricular robotic neck dissection and 32 underwent conventional open neck dissection. Oncological adequacy was assessed by lymph node yield per dissection; quality of life and shoulder function were measured with the Neck Dissection Impairment Index (NDII); and cosmetic outcome was assessed with a structured patient-reported questionnaire. RESULTS: Mean lymph node yield was comparable between the robotic and open groups (23.9 vs 24.6 nodes per dissection; p = 0.542). Mean NDII scores at 3 weeks were similar (65.7 vs 64.2; p = 0.261) and improved over time in both groups. Patient-reported cosmetic satisfaction was significantly higher after robotic neck dissection (12.3 vs 8.0; p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Retro-auricular robotic neck dissection achieves an oncological yield, quality-of-life and shoulder function outcome equivalent to open neck dissection, with a markedly superior cosmetic result, and merits consideration in appropriately selected patients with oral cavity cancer.

item.title: Quantifying the diagnostic time gap in precision oncology: A retrospective analysis of potential time savings from same-day cartridge-based molecular testing versus next-generation sequencing in cytology specimens.
item.dc:creator: Tran K, Chen E, Symmans WF, Sura GH
item.description:
Authors: Tran K, Chen E, Symmans WF, Sura GH
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360239
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886752



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) turnaround times (TAT) exceed two weeks and can delay the initiation of targeted therapy. Rapid cartridge-based platforms such as Idylla deliver single-gene or fusion results from minimal cytology material within hours, but time savings have not been systematically quantified. METHODS: Forty-two cases of non-small cell lung carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, melanoma, and mammary analogue secretory carcinoma of the salivary gland that underwent both Idylla testing (KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, and GeneFusion assays) and orthogonal NGS at a single academic center were reviewed. NGS TAT was calculated from specimen collection to report release, and Idylla results were modeled as available one day after collection. The primary outcome was per-case time savings (NGS TAT minus one day); treatment timelines were reconstructed from the medical record. Analyses were descriptive; no inferential testing was performed. A sensitivity analysis varied the modeled Idylla TAT from 1 to 3 days, and an adjusted estimate assigned no time saving to the two cartridge results that were not actionable on the day of collection. RESULTS: The median NGS TAT across all 42 cases was 20.0 days (IQR, 17.0-23.8; range, 8-51). Against the modeled 1-day Idylla TAT, the median time savings was 19.0 days per case (IQR, 16.0-22.8; range, 7-50), totaling 858 patient-days. Assigning no time saving to those two cases gave a median of 18.0 days and 817 patient-days. No patient received therapy that was subsequently contradicted by the sequencing result. In thirteen patients, the sequencing interval alone exceeded three weeks, and in seven, no systemic therapy was underway while the result was awaited. CONCLUSIONS: Same-day cartridge-based testing from cytology and small biopsy specimens could provide actionable results a median of 19 days earlier than standard NGS. Whether this translates into earlier treatment initiation was not assessed and requires prospective evaluation.

item.title: The relationship between the use of fillers and Japanese proficiency: Focusing on OPI level assessment.
item.dc:creator: Chen Z
item.description:
Authors: Chen Z
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360747
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886675



Abstract:
This study employed a Cumulative Link Mixed Model (CLMM) to examine the relationship between Japanese learners' filler use and OPI (Oral Proficiency Interview) level ratings. The results showed no significant association with proficiency for the i(い)-group, u(う)-group, ano(あの)-group, and eeto(ええと)-group fillers. In contrast, the a(あ)-group, e(え)-group, o(お)-group, and n(ん)-group fillers were significantly negatively associated with higher proficiency, while the use of maa(まあ)-group and sono(その)-group fillers was significantly positively associated with higher proficiency. Furthermore, an analysis of maa(まあ)-group and sono(その)-group fillers based on their functions and discourse roles showed that turn-internal maa(まあ) and inferential/re-presenting sono(その) require at least two clauses to be produced. This indicates a connection with paragraph-level language production, which is one of the criteria for 'Text Type' in OPI assessment. It was also found that the use of these fillers with such functions is significantly positively associated with higher proficiency. On the other hand, for fillers such as ano(あの) and eeto(ええと), as well as maa(まあ) used in adjacency pairs, no significant increase with proficiency was observed, confirming that their use is not associated with paragraph-level production. The use of fillers linked to paragraph-level production can be considered one of the key linguistic factors that can help explain the relationship between filler use and the development of oral language proficiency.

item.title: Molecular screening of selected RNA viruses in neotropical wild felids of Brazil.
item.dc:creator: Colpani M, Duarte-Benvenuto A, Sacristán C, Bueno MG, de Moraes MTB, Zamana-Ramblas R, Codeas BS, Navas-Suarez PE, Arias-Lugo MA, Morato RG, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Colpani M, Duarte-Benvenuto A, Sacristán C, Bueno MG, de Moraes MTB, Zamana-Ramblas R, Codeas BS, Navas-Suarez PE, Arias-Lugo MA, Morato RG, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359169
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886669



Abstract:
Astrovirus, cardiovirus and rotavirus are RNA viruses widely distributed among humans, domestic and wild mammals, including felids, occasionally associated with fatal outbreaks and highly resistant to environmental conditions. Despite this, there are no reports of these viruses in New World felids. The aim of this study was to investigate the presence of astrovirus, rotavirus and cardiovirus in non-domestic felids under human care or in the wild, across multiple Brazilian biomes (i.e., Amazon Forest, Atlantic Forest, Caatinga, and Cerrado). Biological samples (e.g., blood, oral and rectal swabs, and frozen tissues) were submitted to reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for astrovirus detection and real-time RT-PCR for rotavirus and cardiovirus, followed by sequencing. Fifty wild felids were analyzed, comprising 40 free-ranging and 10 captive animals: 19 ocelots (Leopardus pardalis), 12 pumas (Puma concolor), seven jaguarundis (Herpailurus yagouaroundi), six southern tiger cats (Leopardus guttulus), three margays (Leopardus wiedii) and three jaguars (Panthera onca). An astrovirus was detected in rectal swab of a healthy captive southern tiger cat, while a genotype G3P[3] Rotavirus alphagastroenteritidis (Rotavirus A) was detected in intestine of a roadkill puma. All felid samples were negative for cardiovirus. Morphological analyses of available formalin-fixed tissues of the rotavirus-positive puma were inconclusive due to autolysis. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first molecular detection of astrovirus and rotavirus in Neotropical wild felid species.

item.title: Concurrent TMS-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Zhou J, He Y, Jin C, Yang C, Han Y, Wang Y, Zhen Z, Huang Z, Shi S, Che X, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhou J, He Y, Jin C, Yang C, Han Y, Wang Y, Zhen Z, Huang Z, Shi S, Che X, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360250
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886653



Abstract:
Callosal abnormalities disrupt interhemispheric communications that impair the recovery of a series of neurological and psychiatric disorders. Understanding interhemispheric communication could help identify treatments for disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission. This study aimed to validate the sensitivity of a TMS-EEG-based measure of interhemispheric signal propagation (ISP) to GABAB receptor modulation, while independently replicating the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition. A group of 29 participants received an oral dose of either baclofen, a GABAB receptor agonist, or a placebo. Before and after drug intake, single-pulse TMS-EEG was applied to assess ISP in both the motor and prefrontal regions. Our findings indicated that baclofen increased interhemispheric inhibition over the motor region, indexed by significantly decreased ISP (p = 0.037). No significant effect was observed in the dorsolateral prefrontal region (p = 0.186), suggesting regional specificity in GABAB receptor modulation of ISP. These findings uncovered the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition as indexed by ISP. They also highlight the potential of ISP for characterising interhemispheric communication, which could inform the treatment for a series of disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission.

item.title: Multidimensional oral health and frailty in older adults: A sex-stratified cross-sectional study.
item.dc:creator: Yang JE, Moon S
item.description:
Authors: Yang JE, Moon S
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360682
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886645



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty in older adults is a critical public health concern associated with increased morbidity, disability, and healthcare utilization. Although systemic health and socioeconomic factors are well-established determinants of frailty, the multidimensional nature of oral health has received relatively limited attention in previous research. The aim of this study was to examine the associations between general characteristics, health-related factors, oral health factors, and frailty among community-dwelling older adults, and to identify sex differences in frailty. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2022 Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging (KLoSA) and included 3,729 individuals aged 65 years and older. Frailty was categorized as robust, pre-frail, or frail using the Frailty Instrument developed for older Korean adults. General characteristics, health-related factors, and oral health-related factors (structural, behavioral, and subjective) were assessed through structured questionnaires. Hierarchical logistic regression analysis was performed in three steps to identify factors associated with frailty. RESULTS: Of the participants, 16.0% were frail and 84.0% were non-frail (31.5% pre-frail and 52.5% robust). Sex-stratified analyses also showed that structural oral health factors were most strongly associated with frailty in both sexes. Edentulous status without denture use was associated with the highest odds of frailty in both women (OR = 3.76, 95% CI = 3.72-3.80) and men (OR = 2.95, 95% CI = 2.91-2.98). In contrast, sex differences were observed for some subjective oral health factors: tooth sensitivity was associated with higher odds of frailty in women (OR = 1.82, 95% CI = 1.80-1.84) but lower odds in men (OR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.84-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: Oral health conditions, including untreated tooth loss, difficulty in chewing or swallowing, and oral pain, were significantly associated with frailty. These findings suggest that oral health may be an important factor to consider in relation to frailty among community-dwelling older adults.

item.title: Cutaneous Leiomyosarcoma of the Head and Neck: Appreciation of a More Indolent Biological Behavior and Implications for Its Management.
item.dc:creator: de Bree E, de Bree R, Chiesa-Estomba C, Guntinas-Lichius O, Sreeram MP, Michelakis D, Rao KN, Rinaldo A, Ferlito A
item.description:
Authors: de Bree E, de Bree R, Chiesa-Estomba C, Guntinas-Lichius O, Sreeram MP, Michelakis D, Rao KN, Rinaldo A, Ferlito A
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70512
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42885217



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leiomysosarcoma (LMS) is generally associated with high metastatic potential and poor survival. Cutaneous LMS (cLMS) has been considered a different entity with more indolent biological behavior. METHODS: A narrative review was performed to assess the biological behavior of cLMS, with special attention for the head and neck location. RESULTS: cLMS is located in the head and neck in 21%-33%. The local recurrence rate is 2%-18%, while only 3% develops metastatic disease at 10 years. The most important risk factor of recurrent disease is positive/close surgical margins, with a trend for increased risk at the head and neck. The vast majority of recurrences are local and appear during the first few years. No data support adjuvant treatment. The 5-year disease-specific survival is 96%-100%. CONCLUSIONS: cLMS exhibits a moderate risk of local recurrence, low metastatic potential, and excellent disease-specific survival. Surveillance may be focused on physical examination and limited in duration.

item.title: Klebsiella-dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants.
item.dc:creator: Seymour CO, Ecklu-Mensah G, Lee Y, Nicols AR, Cheng WA, Jumarang JM, Marentes Ruiz CJ, Navarro J, Navarro R, Rodriguez-Angeles Y, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Seymour CO, Ecklu-Mensah G, Lee Y, Nicols AR, Cheng WA, Jumarang JM, Marentes Ruiz CJ, Navarro J, Navarro R, Rodriguez-Angeles Y, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78148-x
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42881193



Abstract:
Rotavirus gastroenteritis is the leading cause of infant diarrheal death worldwide. Oral rotavirus vaccine (RVV) prevents illness and death, but efficacy differs between high- and low-income countries and the etiologies are unclear. Here, we describe the relationship between colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, inflammation, and vaccine response across a cohort of infants from Panama, Peru, and the U.S. Vaccine immunogenicity was related to community composition in the first month of life and inverse to increased relative abundance of Klebsiella. Clustering communities into gut types revealed that microbiome configurations with elevated Klebsiella or Escherichia in the first month of life were negatively associated with both seroconversion and rotavirus shedding after vaccination, suggesting potential inhibition of vaccine function or host response. Infants without RVV strain shedding displayed elevated fecal calprotectin in the first month. These results implicate microbiome-augmented infant gut inflammation as a potential impediment to RVV response.

item.title: Transoral robotic versus laser surgery for cT1-T3 supraglottic laryngeal cancers: a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative and non-comparative studies.
item.dc:creator: Lechien JR, Vaira LA, Baudouin R, Guarino P, Chiesa-Estomba CM, Turayeva A, Sagandykova K, Lazzeroni M, Iannella G, Aliyeva A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lechien JR, Vaira LA, Baudouin R, Guarino P, Chiesa-Estomba CM, Turayeva A, Sagandykova K, Lazzeroni M, Iannella G, Aliyeva A, et al.
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108172
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42880162



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare literature findings about functional, oncological and surgical outcomes of transoral robotic (TORS) versus transoral laser microsurgery (TOLM) for supraglottic cT1-T3 laryngeal cancers. METHODS: Three independent investigators conducted a PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library search for papers reporting oncological, functional and surgical (complications) outcomes of TOLM and TORS. Outcomes were statistically compared considering controlled (direct) studies, and indirectly between single-arm cohort studies. RESULTS: Fifty studies (2,644 patients) were included: 19 single-arm TORS (n = 615), 27 single-arm TOLM (n = 1,122), and four comparative studies (n = 907). Pooled positive margins were 7.3% (95%CI, 4.3-12.0) after TORS and 12.7% (8.6-18.3) after TOLM (P = 0.08); the comparative meta-analysis yielded a risk ratio of 0.65 (0.21-1.99; P = 0.45), also favoring TORS non-significantly. No difference was found for postoperative hemorrhage (5.8% versus 6.4%; P = 0.79) or permanent gastrostomy (7.4% versus 4.8%; P = 0.33). Permanent tracheostomy was rare in both groups (1.6% versus 1.3%), and laryngeal preservation reached 99.6% and 93.0%, respectively. Complication rates were not poolable for TOLM (I2 = 87.0%) owing to definitional heterogeneity. Five-year overall survival was 72.6% (65.8-78.4) in the TOLM series and not poolable for TORS. Median follow-up was 26 versus 50 months. CONCLUSION: TORS and TOLM provide currently comparable oncological, surgical, and functional outcomes in cT1-T3 supraglottic LSCC. Direct and indirect evidence converged toward a non-significant margin advantage for TORS. Apparent differences across the literature more plausibly reflect case mix, era, follow-up duration, and outcome definitions than the surgical technique itself. Randomized comparisons in matched populations are critically needed.

item.title: Predicting lymph node metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer using clinical and PET/CT-derived morphological features: An interpretable machine-learning study.
item.dc:creator: Xu Y, Hao J, Dou Y, Zeng B
item.description:
Authors: Xu Y, Hao J, Dou Y, Zeng B
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361043
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42879405



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is crucial for staging and treatment planning. This study aimed to establish a standardized machine learning workflow based on routinely available clinical, serological, and PET/CT-derived parameters to enhance preoperative LNM risk stratification. METHODS: This retrospective study included 255 patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC, all of whom underwent systematic lymph-node dissection. Patients were randomly divided, with stratification by pathological lymph-node status, into a training cohort (n = 178) and an internal held-out test test cohort (n = 77). Candidate predictors were screened using univariable and multivariable logistic regression in the training cohort. Six machine-learning algorithms were trained and optimized using repeated nested five-fold cross-validation. After model development was completed, all six models were applied without modification to the test cohort. Test-set AUCs were compared using paired DeLong tests with Holm correction. The primary model was further evaluated for calibration, clinical utility, and feature contribution using SHAP. A conventional multivariable logistic regression model using the same four predictors was added as a simple reference model, and its discrimination and calibration were compared with those of XGBoost. RESULTS: Central tumor location, elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, elevated squamous cell carcinoma antigen, and solid nodule status were retained as predictors; none of the quantitative PET metabolic parameters remained independently associated with LNM. XGBoost achieved the highest cross-validated AUC among the six candidate machine-learning algorithms in the training cohort (0.735; 95% CI, 0.653-0.813) and was therefore designated the primary model. In the internal held-out test cohort, XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.747 (95% CI, 0.631-0.846). The conventional logistic regression reference model achieved a test AUC of 0.733 (95% CI, 0.612-0.841), with no significant difference from XGBoost (DeLong P = 0.301). Its Brier score was 0.152, compared with 0.198 for XGBoost. CONCLUSION: XGBoost model showed moderate discrimination and a high negative predictive value for pathological LNM in NSCLC. However, its limited positive predictive value and the absence of significant differences among the candidate algorithms support cautious interpretation. External multicenter evaluation is required before clinical implementation.

item.title: Network pharmacology and machine learning reveal kit as a target of roburic acid in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: Preliminary in vitro validation.
item.dc:creator: Tan F, Du H, Deng L, Shen Y, Yang Y, Mei K, Chen Z, Huang Y
item.description:
Authors: Tan F, Du H, Deng L, Shen Y, Yang Y, Mei K, Chen Z, Huang Y
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359087
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42879386



Abstract:
This study aims to systematically explore the potential molecular mechanism of Roburic Acid (RBA) in the treatment of Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma (ATC) through the approaches of network pharmacology, machine learning and in vitro experiments. Public databases were used to retrieve the potential targets of RBA and disease-related targets of ATC. Intersection analysis was performed to identify the common targets, followed by the construction of a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network for these common targets. Enrichment analyses, including GO functional and KEGG pathway analyses, were carried out for the targets. Core targets were further prioritized using SVM, LASSO and random forest machine learning algorithms. Validation of the binding affinity and stability of RBA with the core target was performed using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. Finally, in vitro experiments-including cell viability, scratch assay, apoptosis detection, and Western blot-were conducted using the ATC cell line KHM-5M to validate the therapeutic effect and underlying mechanism of RBA. A total of 401 RBA-associated targets and 2151 ATC-related targets were identified; their intersection yielded 173 shared targets. GO enrichment analysis indicated that these targets were mainly involved in responses to peptide hormones and nuclear receptor activity, among other biological functions. KEGG pathway analysis showed significant enrichment in cancer-related pathways, including the PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways. Using SVM, LASSO regression, and random forest models, KIT was consistently identified as the single core target. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated strong binding between RBA and c-KIT, characterized by low binding energy and the formation of a stable protein-ligand complex. In vitro, RBA significantly reduced KHM-5M cell viability and migration; the inhibitory effect on migration became pronounced at 24 h and was comparable to that of the positive control DOX. Furthermore, RBA promoted apoptosis and dose-dependently suppressed c-KIT phosphorylation. This study integrated network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular simulations to identify KIT as a high-confidence core target of RBA in ATC. Preliminary in vitro validation demonstrated that RBA suppresses ATC cell viability and migration, induces apoptosis, and inhibits c-KIT phosphorylation in a dose-dependent manner.

Authors: Oyoshi W, Murakami T, Tsushima H, Kawamoto K, Igarashi A, Yamaoka S, Fukuda H
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0358693
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42879384



Abstract:
This study aimed to elucidate the impact of preventive dental visits (PDVs) over a 9-year follow-up period on cumulative medical expenditures (MEs) related to lifestyle-related diseases. To this end, the study included 1,891 full-time employees (1,478 males and 413 females), aged 19-57 years, of a manufacturing company in Japan over a 9-year period. This historical cohort study was conducted from 2015 to 2023. The year 2015 served as the baseline, with the subsequent 8 years (2016-2023) used for follow-up. Based on an 8-year dental check-up follow-up survey from 2016 to 2023, participants were classified into two groups, those who reported PDVs in ≥87.5% of the years they answered the survey (regular PDVs) and those who reported PDVs in <12.5% of those years (irregular PDVs). Using 2015 as the baseline, adjustments were made for sex, age, division, Community Periodontal Index, oral health literacy, number of outpatient visits, annual MEs, annual lifestyle-related diseases medical expenditures (LDMEs), lifestyle habits, and health risks. Cumulative LDMEs per capita from 2016 onwards were examined in each group classified as with or without regular PDVs. To adjust for confounding variables between the two groups, we performed a propensity score matching. Although no significant differences in the proportion of individuals incurring LDMEs between the groups with and without regular PDVs, the LDMEs per capita among those who incurred expenditures were significantly lower in the group with regular PDVs. In sensitivity analysis, the threshold for group classification was changed. Specifically, the analysis was conducted with participants who had PDVs in ≥50% vs. those who had PDVs in <50% yielded similar findings as those obtained in the main model. Our results suggest that regular PDVs are associated with moderating LDMEs. These findings may serve as a motivation for promoting preventive dentistry in both corporate and public health initiatives.

item.title: Differences in treatment and outcome of patients with ST- elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI in Germany.
item.dc:creator: Lange SA, Engelbertz C, Makowski L, Dröge P, Ruhnke T, Günster C, Gerß J, Reinecke H, Koeppe J
item.description:
Authors: Lange SA, Engelbertz C, Makowski L, Dröge P, Ruhnke T, Günster C, Gerß J, Reinecke H, Koeppe J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0343889
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42879374



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI (NSTEMI) are very similar regarding pathophysiology and clinical treatments, especially NSTEMI comprises a much more heterogenic group of patients and underlying diseases. We therefore aimed to assess the treatments and outcomes of both entities in a large contemporary cohort. METHODS: Patients with STEMI and NSTEMI between 01/01/2010-31/12/2018 were identified from the largest German health insurance (AOK, ≈ 26 million members). Patient demographics, their hospital course, adherence to guideline-directed drug therapy and overall survival were assessed. RESULTS: In total 544,529 patients (mean age 74, IQR 62-82), one third of whom had a STEMI. Chronic kidney disease, peripheral arterial disease, and heart failure were more common in patients with NSTEMI. Patients with STEMI were more likely to get coronary angiograms and percutaneous coronary interventions. Although STEMI more frequently led to cardiogenic shock, the rate of serious cardiac events was lower. Mortality was higher for STEMI only within the first 30 days, whereas long-term survival rates were better. The combination of statins, angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin receptor blockers, beta blockers, and oral anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents was associated with higher overall survival in patients with STEMI (hazard ratio [HR] 0.21; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 0.20-0.23; p < 0.001) or NSTEMI (HR 0.40; 95%CI 0.38-0.42; p < 0.001). Nevertheless, the prescription rates decreased over time, particular in patients with NSTEMI. CONCLUSION: Clear differences between STEMI and NSTEMI were observed regarding short- and long-term survival. Guideline-recommended therapy improved long-term survival, but decreased during the follow-up period.

item.title: Management of Acquired Velopharyngeal Insufficiency in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Kothari DS, Abiri A, Clair JM, Vukkadala N
item.description:
Authors: Kothari DS, Abiri A, Clair JM, Vukkadala N
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70978
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42878437



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate treatment outcomes for non-cleft, acquired velopharyngeal insufficiency (VPI) in adults and synthesize the efficacy and safety of available interventions. DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from January 2005 to October 2025. REVIEW METHODS: Studies were included if they evaluated interventions with speech and/or swallow outcomes in adults (≥ 18 years) with VPI. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality. Random-effects meta-analysis using logit-transformed pooled proportions determined rates of speech and swallowing improvement. RESULTS: Of 1167 records screened, 11 studies met inclusion criteria, representing 107 adults and 163 interventions. VPI most occurred after head and neck cancer treatment (45%) or neurologic disease (47%). 63.5% had small to moderate VPI. Injection pharyngoplasty (IP) was the most frequently used intervention (82.2%), followed by palatal lift prosthesis (7.4%) and surgical reconstruction (5.5%). Meta-analysis demonstrated improved speech and swallow in 88% (95% CI: 78%-94%) and 78% (95% CI: 49%-93%) across all interventions, and in 88% (95% CI: 73%-95%) and 71% (95% CI: 34%-92%) in IP patients, respectively. IP is effective and has a low 5.2% adverse events rate. CONCLUSION: Acquired VPI in adults is highly treatable, with most patients experiencing improvement in speech and swallowing across interventions. However, evidence remains limited by small sample sizes and heterogeneous outcome reporting. Prospective and comparative studies using standardized diagnostic criteria and uniform outcome measures are required to better define optimal treatment selection for this adult population. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Tumor-Derived DNA Analysis Aids in the Diagnosis of Postpartum Diffuse Midline Glioma.
item.dc:creator: Rodriguez A, Robinson D, Akhavan D, Cunningham D, Larson A, Udhane V, Schilter KF, Nie Q, Reddi HV
item.description:
Authors: Rodriguez A, Robinson D, Akhavan D, Cunningham D, Larson A, Udhane V, Schilter KF, Nie Q, Reddi HV
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag417
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42878416



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gliomas diagnosed during pregnancy or postpartum pose diagnostic and management challenges. Neurologic symptoms may be attributed to physiological changes of pregnancy or the postpartum state, possibly delaying evaluation. When lesions arise in high-risk locations, such as the brainstem, tissue biopsy is frequently infeasible, further complicating the diagnostic process. PATIENT PRESENTATION: A 28-year-old woman developed dysphagia during pregnancy, which persisted and gradually worsened after delivery. Postpartum evaluation identified a right thyroid nodule, subsequently diagnosed as papillary thyroid carcinoma following hemithyroidectomy. Eight months postpartum, the patient experienced progressive dysphagia, headaches, and dizziness. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an expansile medullary lesion concerning for a high-grade primary brainstem tumor. Due to the brainstem location, biopsy was infeasible, and empiric chemoradiation was initiated for presumed high-grade glioma. MOLECULAR FINDINGS: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tumor-derived nucleic acid analysis using Summit™ 2.0 identified an H3-3A K28M alteration, along with co-occurring pathogenic alterations in NF1 and TP53. In conjunction with the clinical and radiographic findings, these molecular results supported classification of the tumor as diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered. MANAGEMENT AND OUTCOME: Following completion of chemoradiation, dordaviprone therapy was initiated. At the most recent documented follow-up in January 2026, brain MRI demonstrated decreased size and enhancement of the medullary lesion, accompanied by improvement in dysphagia, headaches, dystonic movements, balance, and overall performance status. CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates that cerebrospinal fluid-based genomic profiling can provide clinically meaningful molecular information when tissue diagnosis is contraindicated and can inform treatment planning for patients with anatomically inaccessible central nervous system tumors. It also highlights the significance of ongoing evaluation of persistent neurologic symptoms during pregnancy and the postpartum period.

item.title: Cancer Care Navigation Improves Timeliness of Treatment in Head and Neck Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Islam AM, Baldwin RB, Dallas AE, Dyer BJ, Vidwans A, Dunn E, Preziosi C, Elsamna ST, Toman J, Mokhtari T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Islam AM, Baldwin RB, Dallas AE, Dyer BJ, Vidwans A, Dunn E, Preziosi C, Elsamna ST, Toman J, Mokhtari T, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70513
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42877993



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Timely access to oncologic care is critical for patients with head and neck cancer (HNC), yet delays in treatment remain widespread. We sought to determine whether implementation of a care navigation program was associated with improved timeliness. METHODS: Four hunded and four adult patients who underwent HNC resection with free flap reconstruction were retrospectively reviewed. The primary outcome was time to adjuvant therapy and disease-free survival. RESULTS: Median [IQR] age was 64 [58-73] years and 133 (33%) were women. Significant interval decreases were observed from surgery to initiation of adjuvant radiotherapy (56 [39-83] vs. 45 [31-64] days, p = 0.004). Log-rank testing revealed no difference in disease-free survival between pre- and postprogram cohorts (p = 0.7695). CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of a care navigation program was associated with significant reductions in time to treatment. These findings suggest that structured pathways can meaningfully improve oncologic care delivery for HNC patients.

item.title: Long-Acting HIV Therapy in African Adults with Adherence Challenges.
item.dc:creator: Cresswell FV, Kitonsa J, Norcross C, Tumusiime V, Ombajo LA, Garrett N, Kassim S, Owarwo NC, Laker Odongpiny EA, Yawe I, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Cresswell FV, Kitonsa J, Norcross C, Tumusiime V, Ombajo LA, Garrett N, Kassim S, Owarwo NC, Laker Odongpiny EA, Yawe I, et al.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine | DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa2518753
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42874104



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges. METHODS: We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point. RESULTS: A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2). CONCLUSIONS: Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

item.title: Phase 2 Trial of Icotrokinra for Patients with Ulcerative Colitis.
item.dc:creator: Abreu MT, Siegmund B, Surace L, Erondu N, Chen M, Chachu K, Louis E, Matsuoka K, Limdi J, Arthur E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Abreu MT, Siegmund B, Surace L, Erondu N, Chen M, Chachu K, Louis E, Matsuoka K, Limdi J, Arthur E, et al.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine | DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa2604435
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42874103



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monoclonal antibodies targeting the interleukin-23 pathway are effective in treating inflammatory bowel disease. However, these therapies must be administered intravenously or by subcutaneous injection. METHODS: We conducted a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized trial of oral icotrokinra, a peptide that blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. Participants were assigned to receive icotrokinra at a once-daily dose of 400 mg, 200 mg, or 100 mg or placebo. The primary end point was clinical response at week 12. Secondary end points included clinical remission, remission of symptoms, and endoscopic improvement at week 12. RESULTS: A total of 252 participants underwent randomization: 63 were assigned to the 400-mg group, 62 to the 200-mg group, 64 to the 100-mg group, and 63 to the placebo group. All the doses of icotrokinra were superior to placebo with respect to a clinical response at week 12, which occurred in 63% of the participants in the 400-mg group, 58% in the 200-mg group, and 55% in the 100-mg group, as compared with 27% in the placebo group (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo). The percentage of participants with clinical remission at week 12 was also significantly higher in the 400-mg group than in the placebo group (30% vs. 11%, P = 0.006), as were the percentage of participants with symptomatic remission (46% vs. 19%, P<0.001) and the percentage of participants with endoscopic improvement (37% vs. 14%, P = 0.002). Clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 24% of the participants in the 200-mg group (P = 0.054 for the comparison with placebo); in accordance with the fixed-sequence testing procedure to account for multiple comparisons, no further formal testing of secondary end points was conducted. Through week 28, the percentage of participants with adverse events was 60% in the 400-mg group, 66% in the 200-mg group, 66% in the 100-mg group, and 62% in the placebo group. For serious adverse events, the percentages were 2%, 5%, 0%, and 10%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, a clinical response at week 12 was significantly more common with once-daily oral icotrokinra at each of three tested doses than with placebo. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; ANTHEM-UC ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06049017.).

item.title: Evolving role of proton therapy in contemporary oncology.
item.dc:creator: Lebow ES, Shih HA
item.description:
Authors: Lebow ES, Shih HA
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70622
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42870507



Abstract:
Proton therapy offers a distinct physical advantage over photon radiotherapy through the Bragg peak dose concentration in target with both lower integral dose and finite path length, and sharper penumbra as compared to photons, collectively reducing radiation exposure to surrounding normal tissues and potentially improving the therapeutic ratio. However, this advantage is tempered by uncertainties, including range uncertainty and variable relative biological effectiveness. In this review, the authors summarize contemporary evidence supporting proton therapy across pediatric, central nervous system (CNS), head and neck, thoracic, breast, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, and hematologic malignancies, as well as reirradiation. The strength of evidence varies substantially by disease site. Proton therapy is well established in pediatric cancers and selected CNS tumors, where minimizing integral dose and late toxicity is especially important. Randomized trials have demonstrated clinically meaningful benefits in selected settings, including improved disease control and survival with proton craniospinal irradiation for leptomeningeal metastases and reduced toxicity with preserved disease control and survival benefit in oropharyngeal cancer. Conversely, randomized data in localized prostate cancer have not shown improved patient reported outcomes compared with intensity modulated photon therapy. Ongoing phase 3 trials across multiple disease sites are expected to further define the role of protons by clarifying comparative effectiveness, toxicity reduction, and cost-effectiveness relative to advanced photon techniques. Future progress will depend on improved patient selection, robust treatment planning, and emerging technologies including adaptive proton therapy, proton arc therapy, and FLASH radiotherapy.

item.title: Depth of Invasion as a Predictor of Contralateral Nodal Metastasis in Lateralized Oral Tongue Squamous Cell Carcinomas.
item.dc:creator: Sims J, Abdurrob A, Jin J, AlKhoory WL, Shittu K, Chang S, Tam SH, Dang RR
item.description:
Authors: Sims J, Abdurrob A, Jin J, AlKhoory WL, Shittu K, Chang S, Tam SH, Dang RR
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70506
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42876172



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluates the impact of depth of invasion (DOI) on risk of contralateral neck nodal disease (CND) in lateralized oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). METHODS: Retrospective review was conducted using a tertiary care institutional database from 1998 to 2021. Patients with lateralized oral tongue SCC who underwent surgical resection were included and evaluated for CND in both primary and recurrent settings. RESULTS: A total of 103 patients underwent 104 surgical procedures. Recurrence was observed in 30 patients (28.8%), and CND occurred in 20 patients (19.2%). Multivariate analysis identified a DOI threshold of 9 mm as the earliest point of statistical significance. Patients with DOI ≥ 9 mm demonstrated approximately 6.5-fold higher adjusted odds of contralateral nodal disease (95% CI 1.5-27.4, p-value = 0.011). CONCLUSION: In this institutional cohort, increasing DOI was significantly associated with a higher risk of contralateral nodal disease.

item.title: Impact of Surgical Airways on Location of Death, Healthcare Utilization, and Costs Among Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: A Population-Based Study.
item.dc:creator: Pickett AT, Webber C, Pugliese M, Dover K, Tohme A, Johnson-Obaseki S, Tanuseputro P
item.description:
Authors: Pickett AT, Webber C, Pugliese M, Dover K, Tohme A, Johnson-Obaseki S, Tanuseputro P
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70479
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42876170



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with surgical airways experience barriers to high quality end-of-life (EOL) care. Recognizing differences in healthcare utilization and location of death among patients with surgical airways may inform improvements in EOL care delivery. This study aimed to compare location of death and selected aspects of healthcare in the last 90 days of life between head and neck cancer (HNC) patients with and without a surgical airway. METHODS: Retrospective decedent cohort study of health administrative data from the Institute of Clinical Evaluative Sciences in Ontario, Canada of individuals with HNC who died between January 1, 2008, and December 31, 2018. The exposure group included those with a total laryngectomy any time prior to death or emergency tracheostomy within 90 days prior to death. Primary outcomes included location of death and length of stay in hospital, palliative care encounters, and burdensome transitions of care in the last 90 days of life. Secondary outcomes included healthcare costs during the last 90 days of life. RESULTS: Patients with surgical airways (n = 1280, 7.8%) were more likely to die in a subacute care center (OR = 1.51 [95% CI: 1.26-1.81], p < 0.001) than those without surgical airways. There were no significant differences between the groups for deaths occurring in acute care (OR = 1.11 [95% CI: 0.97-1.27], p = 0.14) or long-term care settings (OR = 0.85 [95% CI: 0.62-1.16], p = 0.30). In the last 90 days of life, they spent more time in acute care hospitals (6.37 days [95% CI: 5.40-7.39], p < 0.001), had higher odds of experiencing burdensome transitions (OR = 1.46 [95% CI: 1.29-1.67], p < 0.001) and had greater costs associated with their care (mean cost ratio = 1.43 [95% CI: 1.36-1.51], p < 0.001). However, after adjusting for covariates, there was no statistically significant difference in palliative care involvement between patients with and without surgical airways (OR = 1.14 [95% CI: 0.98-1.31], p = 0.09). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with surgical airways were more likely to die in subacute care centers and experienced increased healthcare utilization, including longer hospital stays, higher rates of burdensome transitions, and greater costs in the last 90 days of life. There was no statistically significant difference in palliative care involvement between groups after adjustment. These findings should be interpreted with caution, as adjustment for disease stage and tumor site was not possible due to missing data. Further research is needed to better understand the underlying drivers of these differences and their implications for EOL care.

item.title: Long-Term Oncologic Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Orbital Exenteration for Advanced Head and Neck Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Patel TM, Vasudevan SS, Nathan CO
item.description:
Authors: Patel TM, Vasudevan SS, Nathan CO
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70517
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42876146



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment of head and neck cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (HNcSCC) with orbital invasion is challenging due to its aggressive local behavior and the limited effectiveness of eye-sparing options in advanced disease. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prognostic outcomes in advanced HNcSCC patients undergoing orbital exenteration (OE). METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to April 30, 2026, for studies reporting survival, tumor control, and complication outcomes in patients with advanced HNcSCC undergoing OE. Pooled estimates were calculated using a random-effects model, with further sensitivity analysis and meta-regression analysis. RESULTS: Ten studies comprising 217 patients were analyzed. Most patients were male (83%); median age was 66.3 years. The pooled 2-year overall survival was 73.7% (95% CI, 63.4%-81.9%) and 5-year overall survival 70.8% (95% CI, 56.0%-82.2%). Pooled 2-year and 5-year disease-free survival were 66.1% (95% CI, 42.2%-83.9%) and 51.6% (95% CI, 37.8%-65.2%). Pooled local and regional recurrence were 23.7% (95% CI, 14.0%-37.1%) and 14.0% (95% CI, 3.9%-39.2%), and the pooled complication rate 39.2% (95% CI, 24.1%-56.7%). In meta-regression, the proportion of margin-positive resections was the only covariate associated with local recurrence (β = 0.076 per percentage point; 95% CI, 0.027 to 0.124; p = 0.015; R2 = 100%); no demographic factor was associated with any outcome. CONCLUSIONS: Patients undergoing OE for advanced HNcSCC had moderate survival and locoregional control with substantial morbidity. Evidence directly comparing OE with orbit-preserving approaches remains sparse, and high-quality comparative studies are needed to define the role of eye-sparing strategies in this high-risk population, particularly in the era of neoadjuvant immunotherapy.

item.title: Selective lipid metabolic remodelling in radiosensitive normal tissues after FLASH radiotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Aramaki S, Dubail M, Sertorio M, Rahman MM, Afroz MS, Zhang C, Tang L, Wakabayashi K, Konishi K, Kahyo T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Aramaki S, Dubail M, Sertorio M, Rahman MM, Afroz MS, Zhang C, Tang L, Wakabayashi K, Konishi K, Kahyo T, et al.
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111825
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42874779



Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: FLASH radiotherapy, delivered at ultra-high dose rates, spares normal tissues while maintaining tumor control, but the molecular basis of this differential response remains poorly defined, particularly at timepoints relevant to tissue repair. We investigated whether lipid metabolism contributes to the FLASH effect in head and neck cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: MOC2 tumor-bearing mice received a single 10 Gy fraction of conventional (CONV) or ultra-high dose-rate FLASH protons, with non-irradiated controls (CTRL). Tongue and contralateral tumors were collected two weeks later and analyzed by bulk lipidomics, spatial lipidomics and proteomics. After biochemical filtering, 1,547 lipid species across 37 classes were quantified. RESULTS: At two weeks, CONV irradiation was associated with a triglyceride-catabolic, oxidative-stress signature in tongue tissue, marked by loss of the lipid-droplet hydrolase Ces1d alongside induction of the peroxisomal β-oxidation enzyme Acox1. FLASH irradiation was instead associated with a distinct lipid-remodelling signature: suppression of Mgll, induction of Apoe, membrane phospholipid remodelling (increased phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine), and Lypla2 upregulation. Spatial lipidomics provided illustrative spatial context consistent with concentration of these changes in minor salivary gland acini. Tumor tissue showed no comparable modality-specific divergence. CONCLUSIONS: These correlative multi-omics data indicate that FLASH is associated with remodelling of lipid metabolism in radiosensitive normal tissue, beyond a simple reduction of acute oxidative damage. We propose a Lipid Metabolic Remodelling Hypothesis for testing: the remodelling of lipid metabolism observed after FLASH may contribute to normal-tissue sparing rather than representing solely a downstream consequence of reduced acute oxidative damage. This model complements existing physicochemical models and offers a basis for radioprotection strategies in head and neck radiotherapy.

item.title: Prognostic significance and predictors of pathological response following neoadjuvant paclitaxel, carboplatin, and cetuximab therapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Suzuki K, Ueki Y, Ohno Y, Ohshima S, Omata J, Yokoyama Y, Takahashi T, Shodo R, Umezu H, Horii A
item.description:
Authors: Suzuki K, Ueki Y, Ohno Y, Ohshima S, Omata J, Yokoyama Y, Takahashi T, Shodo R, Umezu H, Horii A
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108175
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42874320



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy using paclitaxel, carboplatin, and cetuximab (PCE-NAC) is used in patients with locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC); however, predictors of survival outcome remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the pathological response to PCE-NAC and identify clinical factors associated with a favorable pathological response. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 59 patients with HNSCC who underwent PCE-NAC followed by surgery at our institution. Pathological response was assessed according to the General Rules for Clinical and Pathological Studies on Head and Neck Cancer in Japan and categorized as favorable pathological response (≥ Grade 2, less than one-third of cancer cells are viable). Recurrence-free survival (RFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazard analyses. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify the predictors of favorable pathological response. RESULTS: A favorable pathological response (≥ Grade 2) was obtained in 42.4 % of patients, which was significantly associated with better 2-year RFS (80.1 % vs. 62.7 %, p = 0.032). In contrast, pathological complete response and radiological response (complete or partial response) were not significantly associated with prognosis. Multivariable logistic regression analysis determined that younger age and female sex were associated with a favorable pathological response. CONCLUSIONS: Pathological response beyond pCR may provide clinically meaningful information on treatment efficacy following PCE-NAC. Younger age and female sex were associated with a favorable pathological response, suggesting their potential relevance to treatment response.

item.title: Selpercatinib in Pediatric and Adolescent Patients With RET-Altered Solid Tumors: Safety and Efficacy Results From the Phase I/II LIBRETTO-121 Study.
item.dc:creator: Laetsch TW, Kang HJ, Casanova M, Anazodo A, DuBois SG, Manabe A, Navid F, Pappo A, Gilligan AM, Grbovic-Huezo O, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Laetsch TW, Kang HJ, Casanova M, Anazodo A, DuBois SG, Manabe A, Navid F, Pappo A, Gilligan AM, Grbovic-Huezo O, et al.
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology | DOI: 10.1200/JCO-25-03013
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42874021



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Selpercatinib, a highly selective oral RET inhibitor with CNS activity, has previously demonstrated durable responses and an acceptable safety profile in adults with RET-driven cancers. Consequently, the safety and efficacy of selpercatinib were investigated in pediatric/adolescent participants. METHODS: LIBRETTO-121 (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03899792) was a multicenter phase I/II trial of selpercatinib in participants age 0.5-21 years with advanced, RET-altered solid tumors. In phase I, the primary end point was safety, including dose-limiting toxicities. In phase II, the primary end point was objective response rate (ORR) as determined by independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1. Key secondary end points included ORR by investigator, duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, and pharmacokinetics. RESULTS: As of November 8, 2024, 36 participants age 2-20 years were treated with selpercatinib. Tumor types included RET-altered medullary thyroid cancer (MTC, n = 15), RET fusion-positive papillary thyroid cancer (PTC, n = 15), and other (n = 6). The most common treatment-emergent adverse events were diarrhea, nausea, elevated AST, pyrexia, abdominal pain, elevated ALT, headache, cough, and vomiting. No treatment discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events or new adverse drug reactions were observed. ORR by IRC was 53% (19/36; 95% CI, 36 to 70). For participants with MTC and PTC, ORR by IRC was 60% (9/15; 95% CI, 32 to 84) and 53% (8/15; 95% CI, 27 to 79), respectively. The 24-month DOR rate was 100% (95% CI, 100 to 100). CONCLUSION: Selpercatinib showed durable efficacy in pediatric/adolescent participants with RET-altered thyroid cancer and was well tolerated, supporting targeting of RET alterations in pediatric/adolescent patients.

item.title: ACKR3 Establishes a Squamous-Restricted Immune Checkpoint Axis in Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Karatza A, Kumru K, Powell JM, Peng C, Hao Y, Ciampricotti M, Nasias D, Hu H, Elnaggar M, Pour M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Karatza A, Kumru K, Powell JM, Peng C, Hao Y, Ciampricotti M, Nasias D, Hu H, Elnaggar M, Pour M, et al.

Published: 2026-Oct-14

Abstract:
Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) is an aggressive subtype of non-small cell lung cancer with limited targeted therapeutic options and incompletely defined immune-regulatory dependencies. Here, we identified atypical chemokine receptor 3 (ACKR3) as a squamous-enriched regulator that restrains malignant progression in LUSC. Integrative analyses of human LUSC datasets, autochthonous genetically engineered mouse models, and ex vivo organoid systems showed that ACKR3 loss accelerated tumor growth and remodeled the immune microenvironment, marked by reduced CD8⁺ T cell infiltration and increased T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, ACKR3 limited activation of the MIF-CD74-PD-L1 axis, thereby constraining tumor-cell PD-L1 expression and preserving antitumor immune surveillance. In preclinical LUSC models, treatment with the ACKR3-directed PD-L1 degrader KineTAC, a bispecific molecule that co-engages ACKR3 and PD-L1 to promote lysosomal degradation of PD-L1, enhanced antitumor efficacy, particularly in combination with chemotherapy. Together, these findings define ACKR3 as a squamous-associated immune checkpoint regulator and nominate ACKR3-directed PD-L1 degradation as a tumor-selective therapeutic strategy for LUSC.

item.title: Hidden in historical sources: Rediscovering the thorny oyster (Spondylus gaederopus Linnaeus, 1758) in art, archives, and cultural knowledge.
item.dc:creator: Merquiol L, Tribot AS, Faget D, Changeux T
item.description:
Authors: Merquiol L, Tribot AS, Faget D, Changeux T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0356273
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42873758



Abstract:
The thorny oyster (Spondylus gaederopus), a Mediterranean bivalve prised during prehistoric times for its distinctive spiny purple shell, has since been overlooked in cultural and scientific records. Frequently depicted in Early Modern still-life paintings, particularly in Italian works of the seventeenth century, its representations were historically misidentified as scallops or common oysters. This participated in obscuring the visual evidence of occurrence and human use of this species during this period. Here, we adopt an interdisciplinary approach combining art historical analysis, taxonomic verification, archival research, and ethnobiological investigation to reconstruct the cultural and ecological history of S. gaederopus in Italy. We identify the species in 43 paintings dated between 1635 and 1750, predominantly by members of the Neapolitan Recco family, revealing its former abundance in coastal markets. Complementary historical documents, local knowledge, and oral testimonies confirm its culinary and cultural significance across Italy from the Early Modern period to the twentieth and twentieth-first century. Comparative measurements indicate a decline in average shell size since the seventeenth century, consistent with a potential harvesting pressure. Our findings demonstrate that unconventional sources including visual art, archival records, and oral testimonies can provide rich ecological and cultural insights, recovering lost biodiversity references and revealing human-marine interactions over centuries. Integrating such interdisciplinary evidence not only sheds light on the forgotten history of S. gaederopus but also highlights the potential of combining cultural heritage and scientific research to inform contemporary conservation strategies.

item.title: Surgical Management of Killian-Jamieson Diverticulum: A Systematic Review of Open and Endoscopic Outcomes.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review surgical management of Killian-Jamieson diverticulum (KJD) and compare outcomes of open and endoscopic approaches, focusing on symptom control, perioperative recovery, and recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) morbidity. DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to December 1, 2025, with additional Google Scholar and reference screening. REVIEW METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, 2 reviewers independently screened records, selected studies, and extracted patient-level data on surgically treated KJD. Eligible reports described open transcervical or endoscopic treatment with postoperative outcomes. Study quality was appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute checklists, and data were synthesized descriptively by approach. RESULTS: Forty-one studies including 86 patients were analyzed, 47 treated endoscopically and 39 with open surgery. Overall clinical success, defined as symptom resolution or improvement without reintervention, was high in both groups with a failure rate of 3.5%. Complete resolution was reported more often after open surgery, whereas endoscopic treatment more frequently yielded partial improvement. In patients with perioperative data, endoscopic approaches were associated with earlier oral intake and shorter hospital stay, and no mortality was reported. CONCLUSION: Both open and endoscopic surgery for KJD achieve favorable symptom outcomes with low complication rates, and current evidence does not show clear superiority of one approach. Given the rarity of KJD and the small size of existing series, this review provides the most comprehensive synthesis to date of surgical outcomes and perioperative risks across open and endoscopic techniques.

item.title: Glypican-1-Targeted Antibody-Drug Conjugate Exhibits Antitumor Effects Against Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Obata K, Serada S, Suzuki Y, Tuchida K, Miyaguchi J, Funajima E, Yamada H, Naka T
item.description:
Authors: Obata K, Serada S, Suzuki Y, Tuchida K, Miyaguchi J, Funajima E, Yamada H, Naka T
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70514
Published: 2026-Oct-14

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a major health concern with limited therapeutic options. Glypican-1 (GPC1), a heparan sulphate proteoglycan, has been implicated in several malignancies; however, its therapeutic role in OSCC remains elusive. This study investigated the potential of a novel glypican-1 antibody-drug conjugate (GPC1-ADC) conjugated with monomethyl auristatin E as a therapeutic strategy for OSCC. METHODS: GPC1 expression in OSCC tissues was examined by immunohistochemistry using tissue microarrays and by western blotting in OSCC cell lines. The cytotoxicity of GPC1-ADC was assessed using in vitro viability assays, and its effects on the cell cycle and apoptosis were analyzed using flow cytometry and caspase-3/7 activity assays. In vivo antitumor efficacy was evaluated using OSCC cell line-derived and patient-derived xenograft (PDX) mouse models. RESULTS: High GPC1 expression was observed in 78% (39/50) of OSCC cases, whereas normal oral tissues showed no detectable expression. Western blotting confirmed GPC1 protein expression in all the OSCC cell lines tested. GPC1-ADC markedly reduced cell viability in a dose-dependent manner (IC550 = 0.053-0.117 nM), induced G2/M-phase arrest, and activated caspase-3/7, indicating apoptosis. In vivo, high-dose GPC1-ADC markedly inhibited tumor growth in both xenograft and PDX models compared with control treatments, without causing weight loss. CONCLUSION: GPC1-ADC demonstrated potent and specific antitumor activity against GPC1-expressing OSCC in vitro and in vivo. These findings suggest that GPC1-ADC is a promising therapeutic candidate for OSCC and may provide a basis for new treatment strategies; however, further preclinical and clinical evaluation is warranted.

item.title: Real-World Experience With Multimodal Treatment of Resectable Stage II-III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Single Institutional Analysis.

Abstract:
Neoadjuvant therapy has recently become an integral component of multimodal treatment for resectable lung cancer. However, real-world data on perioperative morbidity and treatment adherence remain limited. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of different neoadjuvant treatment approaches applied within daily clinical routine. We retrospectively analyzed patients with resectable stage II-III non-small cell lung cancer undergoing either neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy or chemotherapy/chemoradiotherapy followed by curative surgical resection. Treatment groups were compared with respect to perioperative outcomes, radiologic and pathologic downstaging, and pathologic response. A total of 143 patients met the inclusion criteria, of whom 46 (32.2%) received chemoimmunotherapy and 97 (67.8%) were treated with chemotherapy prior to surgery. Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in only two patients in the chemoimmunotherapy group and four patients in the chemotherapy group. Chemoimmunotherapy was associated with significantly higher rates of pathologic complete response (37.0% vs. 4.1%) and more pronounced nodal downstaging, with a higher proportion of patients achieving ypN0 status (76.1% vs. 34.0%). High tumoral PD-L1 expression (≥ 50%) and squamous cell carcinoma histology were independently associated with pathologic complete response. Real-world treatment with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy was feasible and resulted in improved response rates compared with chemotherapy, without increasing perioperative morbidity. Histology and high PD-L1 expression may serve as predictors for complete pathologic response, although the predictive value of PD-L1 requires confirmation in larger cohorts with more complete biomarker data.

item.title: Orbital Abscess Complicating Allergic Fungal Rhinosinusitis Due to Streptococcus halichoeri: A Rare Zoonotic Sinonasal Infection.

Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261497528

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondary bacterial infections complicating allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (AFRS) are uncommon but can be serious given the expansile nature of the disease which can thin and erode the bone separating the sinuses from the brain and orbits. Zoonotic pathogens are rarely implicated as pathogens. CASE REPORT: A 21-year-old African American male with several years of progressive nasal obstruction, facial pressure, and hyposmia, presented emergently with acute left eye pain and swelling, diplopia, afferent pupillary defect and inferior visual field deficit. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute on chronic sinusitis with a left orbital abscess. The patient underwent emergent endoscopic sinus surgery with left orbitotomy and drainage of the orbital abscess. Intraoperative findings, pathology, cultures, and allergy testing were reviewed demonstrating AFRS and a novel zoonotic bacterium, Streptococcus halichoeri. CONCLUSIONS: This case represents the first otolaryngologic case of S. halichoeri infection, a severe and complicated sinus and orbital infection. It is unclear if the severity of this infection was a consequence of the unusual pathogen, of the long-term thinning of the bone around the orbit, or both. Although AFRS is not considered an infection, secondary bacterial infection may occur and cause severe complications. Early surgical intervention and culture-directed therapy are essential in managing complicated sinonasal diseases.

item.title: Wildfire Air Pollution Exposure and Head and Neck Cancer Incidence.

item.description:

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the association between wildfire-specific particulate matter 2.5 (wPM2.5) exposure and the overall and site-specific incidences of head and neck and aerodigestive cancer (HNC). STUDY DESIGN: Epidemiological retrospective cohort analysis. METHODS: HNC incidence data were derived from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program (2016-2022). The relationship between county-level wPM2.5 exposure metrics and HNC incidence rates were examined using a distributed lag non-linear model, adjusting for health behaviors (tobacco/alcohol use, diet, exercise, and sexual activity), demographics (age, sex, race/ethnicity), population size, and year, with county as a random effect. Lag effects were analyzed over 10 years. HNC subsites included nasal/sinus/ear, nasopharynx, oral cavity, oropharynx (stratified by p16 status), hypopharynx, and larynx. RESULTS: Higher wildfire-specific PM2.5 exposure was associated with increased cumulative HNC incidence over 0-10-year lags, with a cumulative relative risk (cRR) of 1.06 (95% CI: 1.04-1.09) per additional smoke exceedance day, 1.41 (1.24-1.60) for any annual exposure, and 1.23 (1.13-1.33) per percentage-point increase in days above 5 μg/m3. When stratified by p16 status, significant associations were noted for p16-positive, p16-negative, and p16-unknown tumors. CONCLUSIONS: Higher frequency, intensity, or persistence of wildfire-smoke exposure is associated with increased HNC risk, with the strongest associations driven by long-term exposures.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognosis of patients with advanced biliary tract cancer progressing after gemcitabine-based first-line therapy remains poor. Effective second-line treatment options are limited, and outcomes with currently available regimens are modest. Trifluridine/tipiracil (FTD/TPI) and nanoliposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) have demonstrated clinical activity in gastrointestinal malignancies and may provide synergistic antitumor effects. METHODS: TRITICC-2 is an investigator-initiated, prospective, open-label, multicenter, single-arm phase II trial conducted at academic centers in Germany. The study evaluates the efficacy and safety of FTD/TPI in combination with nal-IRI in patients with histologically confirmed, unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer who have progressed on gemcitabine-based first-line therapy. A total of 38 patients are planned for enrollment. Treatment consists of oral FTD/TPI administered on days 1-5 combined with intravenous nal-IRI on day 1 of a 14-day cycle, continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints include overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), safety, and health-related quality of life. An optional translational research program includes serial liquid biopsies and biomarker analyses. Enrollment is ongoing, with recruitment initiated in late 2025. Efficacy, safety, and translational analyses are pending. CONCLUSION: TRITICC-2 investigates a biologically rational combination of FTD/TPI and nal-IRI in a patient population with a high unmet medical need. The study is expected to provide prospective data on the clinical activity and safety of this regimen and may contribute to the identification of biomarkers associated with treatment response in advanced biliary tract cancer. item.title: Intratumoral Immunotherapy-The Future of Treating Merkel Cell Carcinoma?
item.dc:creator: Pande N, Moser JC, Chandrasekaran S, Brohl AS, Kulkarni RP, Ma VT
item.description:
Authors: Pande N, Moser JC, Chandrasekaran S, Brohl AS, Kulkarni RP, Ma VT
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193226
Published: 2026-Oct-07
PMID: 42882919



Abstract:
Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) represents a rare but highly aggressive neuroendocrine skin cancer with limited systemic therapy options for patients who fail or are ineligible for immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Intratumoral (IT) immunotherapy has emerged as a promising strategy, leveraging the accessibility of tumor lesions and their inherent capacity to trigger immune responses, known as abscopal effects. This review synthesizes the current evidence on IT approaches in MCC, including Toll-like receptor agonists, cytokines, and oncolytic viruses, and highlights their distinct mechanisms of action, while emphasizing the critical need for standardized radiographic response assessment of injected and non-injected lesions. Inconsistent documentation of abscopal responses has hindered quantification of IT therapy's systemic potential, particularly in a disease where one-third of patients present with metastases and distant relapse is common. We outline MCC-specific rationale for routine lesion-level tracking, and recommendations for IT trial designs and objectives. Rigorous assessments of abscopal data will clarify IT's role as both rescue therapy and an ICI partner, potentially transforming outcomes in this refractory MCC.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Bleeding is a common concern in dental, oral, and maxillofacial surgery, particularly in patients with increased bleeding risk. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on local and systemic hemostatic agents, including their mechanisms, clinical applications, efficacy, and safety. METHODS: Literature published from January 2020 through November 2025 was reviewed using predefined search terms related to hemostatic agents and surgical bleeding. Clinical studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, guidelines, and consensus statements were considered. Seven clinical cases were also reviewed to demonstrate practical applications of selected hemostatic agents. RESULTS: Mechanical agents provided effective control of routine bleeding, whereas active and flowable agents were useful for persistent or diffuse bleeding. Fibrin-based and combination approaches provided additional support in complex procedures. Tranexamic acid was particularly useful in patients receiving antithrombotic therapy. CONCLUSION: Optimal hemostasis requires a tailored, procedure-specific strategy based on bleeding characteristics, surgical complexity, and patient-specific risk factors.

Abstract:
Patients scheduled for surgery under general anesthesia experience significant stress, including anxiety and fear, partly because of difficulty visualizing the operating room environment; however, preoperative visits to the operating room are often impractical. In oral and maxillofacial surgery, where many patients are young, perioperative anxiety and fear are particularly important issues, yet few studies have evaluated virtual reality (VR)-based operating room visits in this field. We developed a VR-based simulated operating room tour using a three-dimensional video camera to record the transport route from the hospital ward to the central operating room. item.title: From Molecular Alterations to Risk Prediction: Biomarkers of Actinic Keratosis Progression to Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Meyer T, Stockfleth L, Lang K, Käfferlein HU, Brüning T, Stockfleth E
item.description:
Authors: Meyer T, Stockfleth L, Lang K, Käfferlein HU, Brüning T, Stockfleth E
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193221
Published: 2026-Oct-06
PMID: 42882915



Abstract:
The high-and in most countries steadily increasing-incidence of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) represents a growing public health challenge. As the majority of cSCCs arise from pre-existing actinic keratosis (AKs), these lesions are recognized as the principal precursors of invasive disease. A comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms driving the progression from AK to cSCC is essential for advancing prevention, facilitating early diagnosis, and enabling targeted therapies. Moreover, this knowledge provides a basis for identifying biomarkers that can predict the risk of malignant transformation. The progression from AK to cSCC is a complex, multistep process driven by the gradual accumulation of genetic, epigenetic, and microenvironmental alterations. Over the past decades, numerous molecular changes associated with this transition have been identified. However, no single biomarker has demonstrated sufficient predictive accuracy for clinical use. This reflects the pronounced molecular heterogeneity of AKs as no individual alteration is uniformly present in all lesions that undergo malignant progression. In addition, numerous proposed biomarkers are also detected in non-progressive AKs and even in non-neoplastic skin, which compromises their sensitivity and specificity for predicting progression to cSCC. Current evidence, therefore, suggests that the most promising strategy for identifying AKs at greatest risk of malignant transformation is the development of a multi-marker panel. This panel, ideally, should integrate molecular signatures encompassing genetic, epigenetic, proliferative, inflammatory, and microenvironmental markers. This review summarizes the molecular factors that currently represent the most promising candidates for inclusion in such a multi-marker panel and discusses their potential clinical utility, while emphasizing the need for validation in well-designed prospective longitudinal studies.

item.title: Endoscopic Endonasal Approaches to Anterior Cranial Base Meningiomas: Indications, Limitations, and Surgical Decision-Making.
item.dc:creator: Chopra M, John D, Cote DJ, Zada G

Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193217
Published: 2026-Oct-06
